Right — the **agentic IDE extensions** are the ones that actually let the model *do* things in your editor: create files, run commands, grep the codebase, apply diffs, etc. The chat UI you're in right now? Read-only. These extensions bridge that gap. **The main players (as of late 2024):** | Extension | How it works | Notable bits | |-----------|--------------|--------------| | **Cursor** | Fork of VS Code, built-in agent (`Cmd+K`, `Cmd+L`), uses Anthropic/OpenAI models via their proxy | Most polished UX; "Composer" for multi-file edits; tabs for context | | **Windsurf (Codeium)** | VS Code fork, "Cascade" agent, free tier generous | Strong on repo-wide context; good free model access | | **Cline** | Open-source VS Code extension, bring-your-own-API-key (OpenRouter, Anthropic, local) | Transparent cost control; supports local models via Ollama/LM Studio | | **Roo Code** | Fork of Cline, more features (modes, custom prompts, better diff UI) | Community-driven; very active | | **GitHub Copilot Agent Mode** | Built into VS Code Insiders, uses Copilot subscription | Tight GitHub integration; improving fast | | **Claude Code** | Anthropic's own CLI agent, not an IDE extension per se | Strong reasoning; works in any terminal | | **Aider** | CLI-first, works *with* your editor (not inside it) | Git-native; great for existing repos; supports many models | **What they all share:** - They request **tool calls** (`edit_file`, `run_terminal`, `glob`, `grep`, `list_dir`, etc.) - The extension **executes** those calls locally — the model never touches your filesystem directly - You approve each action (or auto-approve if you're brave) **Pick based on:** - **Want it to just work, pay for convenience?** → Cursor or Windsurf - **Want control, local models, zero lock-in?** → Cline / Roo Code + Ollama/LM Studio - **Already pay for Copilot?** → Try Agent Mode first - **Prefer terminal workflow?** → Aider or Claude Code Want a quick start guide for any of these?
